chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The brothers (paternal and maternal) share with the grandfather, meaning the father of the father; the brothers from the father and mother share with the brothers from the father, and the grandfather is like one of the males.

key_terms.اَلْأَبِ وَ اَلْأُمِّ: The father and the mother (indicating full siblings)
key_terms.اَلْجَدِّ: Grandfather (specifically paternal grandfather in this context)

ai.seo_question: How does the grandfather inherit alongside brothers in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib* clarifies the position of the paternal grandfather (Jadd) in the presence of brothers, establishing him as a co-heir rather than being excluded. It specifies that the grandfather's share is calculated as that of a single male (one-third of the brothers' portion if there are multiple, or equal to one brother if there is only one), reflecting the Shia juristic view of 'Qasam' (division) rather than 'Hajb' (exclusion). This ruling is significant in resolving disputes between the Hanafi and Shia schools regarding whether the grandfather blocks the father's descendants or shares with the father's siblings.
